name: Statistical tests of conditional contribution, Bayes-error bounds and ensemble diversity (CPI with knockoffs Watson & Wright 2021; LOCO; Shapley/modality dropout; FeeBee NeurIPS D&B 2021 Bayes error estimators; Wood et al. JMLR 2023 bias-variance-diversity; oracle combination bounds)

inputs_state_output: These are statistical procedures, not tracker architectures: there is no strong/weak branch, memory or fusion point in the tracking sense; the mapping to our setup is by role. CPI [1]: data Z = (X_S, X_R, Y); X_R is the reduced (base) set, X_S the block under test; one model f is trained on all features, then X_S is replaced by knockoffs X~_S that keep the joint covariance with X_R but carry no extra information about Y; output = per-unit loss difference Delta_i = L(f, z~_i) - L(f, z_i), CPI = mean(Delta). LOCO [3] / VIM [4]: refit the learner without the block and compare predictiveness (loss, accuracy, AUC, deviance) on held-out data; [4] defines the population contrast between oracle predictiveness with all features and without the block. SHAPE [6]: modalities are Shapley players, utility = model accuracy, a missing modality is replaced by zeros. FeeBee [7] / GHP [8]: input = feature vectors and class labels; output = lower and upper estimates of the Bayes error rate (BER). Wood et al. [11]: input = predicted distributions of ensemble members; output = decomposition of ensemble loss into average member loss minus diversity (ambiguity). Ours: base X_R = appearance block B of scripts/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026.py (frozen MASA-R50 RoIAlign cosines to snapped exemplar, previous target, bank, 32 PCA products, geometry8, tags and neighbour-relative versions); added X_S = FlyVis activity of a bounded grey crop (F1[...,8:] = 34 output types incl. T4/T5 plus neighbour means, plus relative keys), with the temporal state over exemplar+search frames already collapsed into these saved numbers; label = ident (region is our target); decisions are per query (8326 query rows x 18 candidate slots in train26_features_D.npz), stage 1 identity -> stage 2 gate -> argmax over alternatives with a calibration threshold; utility = mean over videos of (helpful - harmful)/known queries. Key mismatch: all sources assume i.i.d. units with a per-unit loss; our units are clustered by video and track, and utility is a query-level argmax+threshold functional. Therefore the unit of analysis must be the query (or a target-versus-distractor pair) and all resampling must be by video.
fusion_and_training: No source trains a fused model of a strong and weak branch; they evaluate fusion. [1] trains one learner on the full feature set and never retrains: knockoff substitution measures the reliance of that trained model on the block (algorithm-specific), with second-order Gaussian knockoffs in all simulations (knockoff package 0.3.2) and any learner (LM, random forest 500 trees, ANN 20 hidden units, SVM). [3] retrains without the covariate on one half of a split (LOCO), [4] combines K-fold cross-fitting (to allow flexible learners) with sample-splitting (disjoint data for the full and reduced predictiveness, needed for valid tests when the true importance is zero). [6] evaluates trained fusion models with a missing modality set to zero (no retraining), which puts the model off-distribution - the same objection that [14] raises against plain permutation importance with correlated features. [11] analyses combiners: arithmetic mean, normalized geometric mean (= logit averaging, 'product rule') and majority vote; diversity must be managed, not maximised. Mapping to our hybrid: our concatenation of FlyVis features into one gradient-boosting model is early fusion; CPI on it answers 'does the trained hybrid use the fly block', LOCO/VIM answers 'can any refit learner extract value from it given appearance', and the diversity decomposition answers 'would late fusion of a separate fly scorer with the appearance scorer help'. Preventing the weak block from being ignored is not a topic of these sources; [6] only reports (abstract) that multimodal models tend to rely on the dominant modality when modalities are complementary, and use cooperation only when modalities are indispensable.
labels_and_loss: [1]: any per-unit loss; simulations used MSE and MAE (regression) and cross-entropy and misclassification error (classification); the authors note that a first-moment loss ignores higher-moment information and recommend likelihood-based losses to recover the Markov blanket; AUC needs a per-fold variant. [3]: excess absolute (or squared) prediction error, median inferred with sign or Wilcoxon tests on the held-out half. [4]: predictiveness measures R-squared, accuracy, AUC, deviance/cross-entropy. [7]/[8]: multi-class labels with priors; FeeBee injects symmetric label noise rho and uses Lemma 3.1: BER(rho) = BER + rho(1 - 1/C - BER). [11]: squared, cross-entropy with one-hot labels, 0/1. For our use: (i) row log-loss on ident (928 positives of 5345 identity rows on train26, 17.4 percent, report.json identity.base); (ii) query-level choice log-loss after a softmax over the candidates of a query (the quantity the argmax policy actually uses); (iii) a target-versus-hardest-distractor pair label with random sign, which makes classes exactly balanced and is the natural unit for 'confusable pairs' (hard negative = the candidate with the highest MASA cosine to the exemplar other than the target, chosen without labels on the appearance side); (iv) the per-query utility net in {-1, 0, +1} used as a loss for a utility-level CPI. Class imbalance is handled by (iii) and by priors in the BER bounds.
data_camera_resolution_rate: [1]: simulated Gaussian predictors with covariance 0.5^|i-j|, n = 1000, p in {10, 20, 50}, linear and nonlinear outcomes, 10,000 replicates; Boston housing (506 rows, UCI); breast-cancer gene expression (BLBC). [7]: MNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100, IMDB, SST2, YELP with pre-trained feature transformations (embeddings, PCA). [8]: synthetic Gaussian mixtures and benchmark data [uncertain: exact real datasets]. [11]: MNIST and standard regression/classification benchmarks with bagging and random forests. [4]: HIV-1 antibody study plus simulations. [6]: multimodal benchmarks such as VQA and CMU-MOSEI. None uses video, tracking, camera motion, frame rate or lighting variation. Ours (for the precheck): BDD100K MOT train-split videos; fit104 = fit84 + fit20 (model fitting and calibration, reused many times) and train26 (evaluated once for this hybrid configuration); train26 has 5345 identity rows with 928 positives and 26 independent videos, which bounds statistical power.
metrics_and_numbers: Authors' numbers (not transferable to our utility): [7] Table 3, optimal lower-bound sub-optimality L_D (lower is better): CIFAR10 kNN 0.03, kNN-LOO 0.03, 1NN 0.05, GHP 0.07, KDE 0.36; CIFAR100 kNN 0.06, 1NN 0.14, GHP 0.20; SST2 1NN 0.32, GHP 0.44; upper-bound sub-optimality U_D: CIFAR10 kNN 0.15, 1NN 0.37, GHP 0.39; SST2 1NN 0.63, GHP 0.73 (upper bounds from 1NN/GHP are poor). [7] Table 4: 1NN and GHP are the only estimators whose hyper-parameters/transformation chosen by minimising the estimate at rho = 0 are also near-optimal for L_D (differences 0.00-0.01). [7] section 4.3: the framework becomes unreliable when the best known classifier is weak (YELP, 27.80 percent error). [7] code methods/ghp.py: delta = (dichotomous MST edges)/(2n); upper = 2*delta; lower = ((C-1)/C)(1 - sqrt(1 - 2C/(C-1)*delta)). [7] eq. 2 (from [10]): BER_lower = e_1NN / (1 + sqrt(1 - C/(C-1) * e_1NN)); for C = 2 this equals (1 - sqrt(1 - 2 e))/2. [8] eq. 10-11 (binary HP bound): 1/2 - 1/2 sqrt(u) <= BER <= 1/2 - 1/2 u, u = 4pq D + (p - q)^2. [1] section 4.1: Type I error controlled for all four learners with CE and misclassification loss; Fisher test slightly more powerful than t-test; 10,000 permutations; CPI less powerful than the knockoff filter at feature autocorrelation > 0.5 (Fig. 3); 49 h to generate second-order knockoffs for the gene-expression matrix (section 5). [11] eq. 25-26: majority-vote 0/1 loss = average member loss - y*q-weighted disagreement (good minus bad diversity); Theorem 10: no label-independent diversity effect exists for 0/1 loss with any combiner; Corollary 9: expected cross-entropy = average bias + average variance - diversity for the normalized geometric mean. Our own numbers used by the recipe (source runs/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026/report.json): paired.true_identity-baseline +2.836 pp [1.873; 3.831]; paired.base-baseline +0.660 [0.035; 1.302]; paired.base_D-base +0.106 [-0.176; 0.400]; base_D-base_R1 -0.042 [-0.358; 0.280]; base_D-base_C -0.095 [-0.403; 0.228]; identity AUC base 0.9646, base_D 0.9728, base_C 0.9714, base_R1 0.9708 (n 5345, positives 928); counts (selected/beneficial/harmful): true_identity 721/321/154 (net +167), base 332/137/98 (net +39), base_D 305/129/84 (net +45), base_R1 240/112/58 (net +54), base_C 293/127/70 (net +57). Computed here from per_video: SD over 26 videos of base_D - base = 0.768 pp (SE 0.151 pp), of base_D - base_R1 0.858 pp, of true_identity - base 1.778 pp.
distinguishing_ablations: None of the sources tests a motion or bio-inspired branch over strong appearance; there is no tracking ablation to cite. What they provide are controls with known behaviour: [1] the knockoff copy is an in-model null twin of the tested block (same marginal and joint structure with X_R, no extra information about Y); simulations show controlled Type I error and nominal coverage, but reduced power when the tested features are strongly correlated with the rest (autocorrelation > 0.5) - exactly our case, since FlyVis output is a deterministic function of the eye input R1 and correlates with appearance and geometry. [4] sample-splitting is required for valid inference when the true importance is zero, and the delta-null H0: importance in [0, delta] allows testing for a practically relevant effect rather than any nonzero effect. [5] shows by worked examples that LOCO goes to 0 when a feature is perfectly predictable from the others while its Shapley value stays large - Shapley does not remove correlation. [7] validates estimators by a label-noise ladder (known BER evolution, Lemma 3.1) and finds KDE, DE-kNN and kNN-Extrapolate unreliable and 1NN/GHP upper bounds loose. [11] shows diversity can increase error ('bad diversity') and that larger, less diverse members can beat a more diverse ensemble (Fig. 7 discussion). Negative/limiting results relevant to us: no conditional-independence test is uniformly valid (Shah-Peters no-free-lunch, cited in [1] section 5), and no algorithm efficiently produces nontrivial knockoffs for arbitrary distributions (Bates et al., cited ibid.). Our own distinguishing ablation already exists for one learner (base / base+D / base+C / base+R1 on train26, report.json) and gave no fly-specific gain; these procedures add equal-capacity random-block arms and maximal-gain (headroom) estimates, which the existing ablation lacks.
explanations_addressed: (1) Fly carries no unique identity information beyond appearance: directly testable (method, not evidence) by refit-based LOCO/VIM with a delta-null [3][4], by query-level pair Bayes-error bounds with and without the fly block [7][8][10], and by the complementarity headroom (queries where the fly-informed ranking is right and appearance is wrong). Our existing AUC gain (0.9646 -> 0.9728) closed about 23 percent of the AUC gap to 1 but only about 5 percent of the net-query headroom (+6 of 128 net queries, counts in report.json), so AUC over all rows is a poor proxy and the tests must be done at the query level. (2) Information exists but fusion/training ignores it (modality imbalance): distinguishable by contrasting CPI on the trained concatenated hybrid (reliance) with LOCO/VIM after refit and with a late-fusion diversity check [11]: if refit or late fusion shows value but CPI of the boosting hybrid is near 0, the problem is fusion; if all are near 0, it is redundancy. [6] is only a design analogy (dominant-modality reliance). (3) Saved readout features lost the information; new activity or a fine-tuned core is needed: these tests cannot settle it on saved features alone - caution. By the data-processing inequality the Bayes error of (appearance, any FlyVis_theta(crop)) is never below that of (appearance, crop sequence), so the only valid upper bound for core fine-tuning is the value an unconstrained, equal-or-larger model extracts from the same crop sequence over appearance. (4) FlyVis lacks the lobula/LC object pathway: not addressed; the same tests can evaluate a future lobula-like output block. (5) Motion helps only in subsets diluted by averaging: addressed through pre-registered slice tests and dilution arithmetic (overall gain <= slice share x slice gain); delta-null per slice with Holm correction. (6) Ceiling too low: directly addressed. Perfect identity gives +2.836 pp over the bench and +2.175 pp over appearance on train26; the minimum detectable fly-over-appearance effect with 26 videos is about 2.8 x 0.151 = 0.42 pp (80 percent power, two-sided 5 percent), so any mechanism whose headroom upper bound is below 0.42 pp cannot pass the pre-registered test, and reaching the +2 pp problem criterion needs roughly 62 percent of the identity headroom [uncertain: pooled-count approximation of a per-video metric].
evidence_strength: All core methods are peer-reviewed: [1] Machine Learning 2021, [3] JASA 2018, [4] JASA, [5] Statistical Science 2024, [6] IJCAI 2022, [7] NeurIPS 2021 D&B, [8] IEEE TSP 2020, [11] JMLR 2023. Code existence verified for FeeBee (ghp.py read), Decompose, vimp, cpi, conformal. Independent replication: FeeBee [7] is an independent empirical comparison of the 1NN and GHP estimators; the LOCO family is one line of work. Overall: strong as statistical methodology under i.i.d. assumptions; moderate for our decision, because our data are clustered (26 videos), Bayes-error estimators are asymptotic and loose in 100+ dimensions with a few hundred to a few thousand pairs, and knockoff construction for a 200-dimensional correlated block is approximate. They give no empirical evidence about motion versus appearance.
difference_from_tried: Tried so far: realised-gain comparisons of one learner (gradient boosting on concatenated features) - identity AUC per arm and paired video bootstrap of utility for base, base+D, base+C, base+R1, once on train26 (report.json); fit104 numbers reused for selection. Not tried: (a) a headroom estimate - the maximal utility the fly could deliver if trusted exactly where it ranks the target correctly and appearance does not (complementarity oracle), and the partial-truth utility curve that converts fixed identity errors into pp; (b) refit-based conditional importance with a delta-null at the detectable effect size; (c) knockoff/conditional-permutation reliance of the trained hybrid, including utility-level CPI; (d) Bayes-error lower bounds on target-versus-distractor pairs with and without the fly block and with equal-capacity null blocks; (e) the cross-entropy diversity condition for late fusion of separate appearance and fly scorers; (f) the data-processing bound for core fine-tuning via a rich eye-input model. The difference is that these predict the maximum achievable gain and permit stopping before GPU, whereas our previous tests measured only what one learner realised.
math_precheck: READY RECIPE (CPU, saved features, no FlyVis training). P0 Setup: rebuild the matrices exactly as scripts/z13_hybrid_fly_confirm_20261026.py (B = appearance block; arms D, C, R1 = F1[...,8:] + relative keys). Add two null arms of equal width: RAND = D permuted between queries within the same video (keeps marginals, destroys alignment) and GAUSS = Gaussian block with the covariance of D. Unit = query; groups = video. All estimation on fit104 with 5-fold video-grouped cross-fitting; train26 used only once, with frozen choices, for confirmation (it already served one evaluation of this configuration). P1 Headroom ladder (utility, no new learners): reuse policy_net (scripts/z13_identity_gate_readout_20261026.py lines 181-187) and the stage-2 gate. U(S) = utility when the stage-1 identity probability is set to the truth on query set S and left at the appearance-arm value elsewhere, gate threshold re-chosen on calibration videos. Compute U(all) (must reproduce +2.84 on train26 / +2.93 on fit104), U(empty) = appearance arm, U(S_comp(F)) with S_comp(F) = queries where the appearance argmax is wrong and the A+F argmax (or F-only argmax) is right, for F in {D, C, R1, RAND, GAUSS}; and the random-fix curve U(pi) where a random fraction pi of appearance identity errors is set to truth (20 draws). Headroom H(F) = U(S_comp(F)) - U(empty) with video bootstrap (5000). Arithmetic anchors from report.json: perfect identity net +167 queries vs base +39 (headroom 128 net queries ~ +2.18 pp); base_D realised +6 net (+0.106 pp); minimum detectable effect over appearance on 26 videos MDE = 2.8 x SE = 2.8 x 0.151 = 0.42 pp, about 25 net queries; +2 pp over bench needs ~118 net, i.e. ~79 more than base [uncertain: pooled-count approximation]. STOP-1: upper 95 percent bound of H(D) < 0.42 pp -> no use of the saved fly block can pass the pre-registered test; stop the saved-feature line. STOP-2 (fly specificity): lower 95 percent bound of H(D) - H(R1) <= 0, or of H(D) - H(RAND) <= 0 -> fly's uniquely-right set is not larger than eye input or a null block of equal width; no fly result is possible. Record (not a stop for fly-vs-no-fly) whether U(empty) + H(D) can reach +2 pp. Note H is optimistic (it assumes knowing where the fly is right). P2 Pair Bayes-error bounds [7][8][10]: for every query with >= 2 labelled candidates, pair the target with its hardest distractor (highest MASA cosine to the exemplar). Features = differences of out-of-fold scores, 1-D (ds_A) versus 2-D (ds_A, ds_F), with random sign and label = sign (balanced, C = 2). Low dimension makes 1NN and MST estimates usable with hundreds of pairs. Estimators: 1NN leave-one-out error e and GHP dichotomous-edge rate (FeeBee ghp.py); lower bound LB = (1 - sqrt(1 - 2e))/2, asymptotic upper bound UB = e. Repeat on standardized PCA-k blocks (k = 8-16) of raw A and A+F to check that score collapse lost nothing (by data processing, BER(scores) >= BER(features)). Validate each estimator with the FeeBee ladder: flip rho in {0.1, 0.2, 0.3} of pair labels and require the estimate to follow BER + rho(1/2 - BER) within its bootstrap band; discard estimators that do not. Monotonicity check: a true BER never increases when features are added; an increase means estimator bias from dimension, not harm. Maximal pair-error reduction from F <= e_A(held-out best appearance pair classifier) - LB(A,F). Convert pair-error reduction into net queries with the P1 random-fix curve. STOP-3: if e_A - LB(A,D) converts to < 0.42 pp, stop. Because lower bounds are loose ([7] Table 3), a non-stop here is NOT evidence of benefit; only the stop direction is decisive. P3 Conditional tests (the decision estimand is conditional: 'is D needed given A'; Shapley is not, per [5]). (a) VIM/LOCO with refit [4] Algorithm 3: predictiveness = query-level choice log-likelihood (and top-1 accuracy) on confusable queries; disjoint video halves for full (A+D) and reduced (A) fits, cross-fitting inside each half; delta-null with delta = the predictiveness change that P1 maps to 0.42 pp; repeat for D given (A, R1) and for RAND (must be non-significant; it is the calibration of the test). (b) CPI [1] on the trained hybrid: replace D by a conditional knockoff given A and geometry (second-order Gaussian knockoff on PCA-20 of D conditional on PCA of A, or conditional permutation [15] of D within deciles of the appearance score inside each video); Delta_q = loss(knockoff) - loss(original) per query, averaged per video, video bootstrap; also with the utility net as loss, which gives reliance directly in pp. Low CPI power under strong correlation is expected (their Fig. 3), so CPI alone never stops the line; CPI ~ 0 with VIM > delta diagnoses fusion failure (imbalance) rather than redundancy. (c) Shapley over {A, G, F} (8 refits) only as a descriptive table, never for the decision. P4 Late-fusion diversity [11] [12] [13]: for fixed held-out choice distributions q_A and q_F over the candidates of each confusable query, the normalized geometric mean q = Z^-1 sqrt(q_A q_F) satisfies CE(q) = 1/2 CE(q_A) + 1/2 CE(q_F) - 1/2[KL(q||q_A) + KL(q||q_F)] (ambiguity form of Corollary 9 for fixed members); late fusion beats appearance only if the ambiguity term exceeds 1/2(CE_F - CE_A); report also good versus bad disagreements (F right and A wrong vs A right and F wrong) with an exact McNemar test [16]. STOP-4: good <= bad for D, or D not better than R1 on the same counts -> no late-fusion route. P5 Bound for core fine-tuning: saved features cannot bound a fine-tuned core. Train a small unconstrained probe of equal or larger capacity than FlyVis (e.g. a 2-layer MLP or GRU over the eye-input crop sequence R1 at FlyVis resolution) on identity given A and compute H(R1-rich) with P1. STOP-5: upper bound of H(R1-rich) < 0.42 pp -> no FlyVis_theta(crop) can help either; do not launch GPU fine-tuning. GO to GPU only if all hold: (i) H(R1-rich) or H(D) point estimate >= ~1 pp with lower bound > 0.42 pp; (ii) the VIM delta-null is rejected for fly-given-appearance overall or in a pre-registered slice; (iii) H(D) exceeds H(RAND) and H(R1) for the saved-feature route, or, for the fine-tuning route, the equal-capacity unconstrained control is pre-registered as arm (2). Otherwise stop. If confidence intervals straddle thresholds, record 'inconclusive' and do not move to GPU.
cue_role_and_regime: The procedures are regime-agnostic; the regime must be supplied by pre-registered slices. Role tested: the fly block as an added feature (VIM/CPI), as a separate late-fusion scorer (diversity condition), or as an identity override on queries where it is right (headroom oracle, an optimistic gate). Recommended slices, defined without labels and fixed on fit104: similar look (MASA cosine margin between the top-2 candidates below a threshold), crossing paths (IoU between candidate boxes above a threshold), occlusion (frames since the last confirmed match), darkness (low mean crop luminance) and glare (high saturated-pixel fraction). Dilution arithmetic: if a slice holds a share s of the helpful queries, the overall gain is at most s times the slice gain; for example a slice with 20 percent of helpful queries must give about 2.1 pp inside the slice to deliver the 0.42 pp detectable overall effect. Slice tests use Holm correction; a gain in a non-BDD100K regime or on another dataset says nothing about ours.
no_fly_equivalent_control: Required arms for every test above: (1) appearance only (base B); (2) appearance + eye input R1 of the same crop (the strongest no-fly control, since FlyVis output is a function of that input); (3) appearance + stock FlyVis C (modernisation control); (4) appearance + equal-width null blocks: RAND (D permuted between queries within each video) and GAUSS (Gaussian block with D's covariance) - these calibrate the bias of adding dimensions to boosting, 1NN and MST estimators; (5) appearance + simple motion cues of equal width without FlyVis (velocity direction consistency, Kalman innovation, IoU with the tracker prediction); (6) for the fine-tuning bound, an unconstrained MLP/GRU of equal or larger parameter count on the same crop sequence. A fly result needs (A+D) > (A+R1) and (A+D) > (A+RAND) with a positive lower bound.
bio_node_mapping: No biological node is implied by these sources. The tests apply to whatever FlyVis node produces the block: current readout of T4a-d/T5a-d and the other 34 output types with neighbour means (motion pathway, medulla/lobula plate level), and later to a lobula/LC-like or STMD-facilitation output layer built from FlyWire 783 connectivity. They are the measurement layer that decides whether a node change is worth GPU time.
novelty_overlap: Applying conditional importance tests, pair Bayes-error bounds and a utility headroom oracle to decide whether a connectome-constrained motion model adds identity information beyond strong appearance in MOT was not found in the sources examined [uncertain: no targeted search]; the methods themselves are standard, so any claim is about the application, not the method.
candidate_node_change: The sources gate which node change to fund rather than proposing one. Decision mapping: (a) H(R1-rich) passes but saved D does not -> the information is in the input but lost by the current FlyVis readout/core: fund core fine-tuning on identity (input preparation + connections/parameters + readout, the prepared script) with arms: appearance only, appearance + stock C, appearance + eye input R1, appearance + equal-capacity unconstrained network on the same crop, appearance + fine-tuned FlyVis; proceed to GPU only if STOP-5 is passed and the unconstrained control is pre-registered. (b) H(D) and VIM pass but the concatenated boosting CPI is near 0 and realised gain is small -> fusion failure: change the readout node (learned low-dimensional projection of FlyVis activity added with alpha = 0 at start to the MASA similarity, see C01) and test against the same projection on R1 and on RAND. (c) H(D) <= H(R1) and H(R1-rich) < 0.42 pp -> stop the identity role of FlyVis on this bench; record a negative result for this implementation, name the failed node (identity information absent beyond appearance at the crop level) and move FlyVis to another role. Why this fixes a FlyVis problem: it targets the measured saturation of FlyVis identity (AUC 0.950-0.956 alone, D = stock C, no gain over R1) by first establishing whether any crop-level model can carry the missing information.
strongest_objection: Everything here measures information in the saved features under the chosen learners and with 26 confirmation videos: (1) a null result cannot rule out benefit from a different representation (fine-tuned core, new activity, lobula pathway) - only the rich eye-input bound P5 addresses that, and only if the probe is strong enough; (2) the headroom oracle is optimistic and the Bayes-error lower bounds are asymptotic and loose ([7] shows 1NN/GHP upper-bound sub-optimality 0.37-0.73), so 'go' signals are weak; only 'stop' signals are reliable; (3) with MDE about 0.42 pp, 'no effect' means 'no effect larger than about 0.4 pp', not zero; (4) fit104 has been reused many times and train26 once, so prechecks must not be tuned on train26 or its confirmatory value is lost; (5) knockoffs for a 200-dimensional block that is a deterministic function of R1 are approximate, and CPI power drops under such correlation.
cost_and_hardware: CPU only for P0-P4: policy re-runs with substituted identity scores take seconds to minutes per arm; pair 1NN/GHP on a few thousand pairs needs an O(n^2) distance matrix (seconds) plus the label-noise ladder and bootstraps (minutes); cross-fitted VIM with gradient boosting, 5 folds x 2 halves x 6 arms, roughly 0.5-2 h on 3 threads [uncertain]; conditional knockoffs on PCA blocks minutes. P5 needs the eye-input crop sequences: if only summary R1 features are saved, rebuilding sequences is a CPU data-loading job of hours and the small probe trains on CPU or briefly on the 12 GB GPU; no FlyVis core training is required for the precheck.
